notes:
Summary: Rivergate Sentry Labs (mid-market SaaS, customer support + intelligent search). Initially tried Hosted API for embeddings + doc-search; now evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation. Key ask: enterprise-grade SLA, VPC deployment, EU data residency for subset of customers.

POC and performance: POC ran on a 4-GPU dedicated cluster (Q4 POC). Observed: average embedding latency 60-80ms; batched reranking end-to-end median 180ms at steady state. Under synthetic burst tests (500 rps for 30s) saw queuing; Redwood suggested burst capacity and auto-burst pool. Customer wants hard SLO of 200ms for 90th pct for chat/rerank paths.

Pricing/Packaging negotiation (current focus):
- Customer preference: fixed monthly commit for predictable unit cost with explicit burst allowance.
- AE proposal v1 (10/30): 3 commit tiers: 40% commit (base) / 70% commit / 100% commit of target baseline GPU-hours. Each tier includes a defined burst credit pool (hours per month) and overage price-per-GPU-hour.
- Customer counter: wants steeper ramp schedule (Q1 50% -> Q2 80% -> Q3 100%) and lower overage ceilings (capped $/hour above commit up to 20% of usage).
- Specific asks from procurement: 12-month contract with quarterly ramp credits, one-time onboarding credit, optional 6-month evaluation extension, automatic cost reconciliation for months under commit.
- Overage mechanics discussed: Redwood proposed tiered overage: first 10% overage billed at 1.25x commit rate, next 10% at 1.5x, beyond that at 2x; Rivergate pushing for 1.15x / 1.35x / 1.8x.
- Burst behavior: Redwood to guarantee immediate burst up to X GPUs for short windows (configurable), with throttling policy and prioritized fallback to hosted API model variants to maintain SLOs. Rivergate requested guaranteed minimum burst of 2 GPUs sustained for 5 minutes and soft-burst for longer tails.
- Ramp schedule: discussed staged increases and true-up credits. Rivergate wants formal ramp schedule in contract with abort/change flexibility tied to monthly usage metrics.

Security/compliance: Rivergate requires SSO/SAML, SOC2, audit logs surfaced in Console, and KMS integration (bring-your-own-key). Data residency: EU customer profiles must remain in eu-region VPC nodes; Redwood proposed tenant-aware routing + model variants.

Ops/Integration notes: SE (Priya) worked with Rivergate infra to map VPC peering and private endpoint; network egress concerns flagged (bandwidth estimates). POC uncovered need for prefix caching for retriever vector store to hit latency targets.

Quotes/voice of customer: "We need cost predictability but can't compromise latency during support spikes — that's our CX SLA." — Head of Product. Procurement: "We can commit if ramp and overage guardrails reduce tail cost risk."

Open items: final commit % and price per GPU-hour, exact burst pool sizing and billing rules, formal legal language on data residency / audit responsibilities, SOC2 evidence delivery timeline.

Next steps: 1) AE to send updated term sheet with revised overage bands and proposed ramp schedule (by 2025-11-07). 2) SE to provide updated network diagram + estimated egress cost (by 2025-11-06). 3) Legal teams to exchange redlines on data residency clause (start 2025-11-10).
